test_contract:
This is a context item, so there is no runtime contract and no test file to add — inventing one would violate AGENTS.md's ban on placeholder tests. The contract is different in kind: every anchor in this ledger must be REPRODUCIBLE by a real command, and the gate is a re-runnable assertion script (below) that exits non-zero if any anchor drifts.

The consumer is a human engineer on Monday who will type the plan's line numbers into an editor. If a line number in this ledger is wrong, they open the wrong function and spend ~an hour before noticing. If the gate is not fail-able, a wrong ledger looks exactly like a right one. That is the whole reason the gate below exists and the reason it is stated as executable assertions rather than prose.

What the engineer sees if this item regresses: they edit `extension-ui-controller.ts:148` expecting `setHeader` and land in the middle of `setTheme`; they add `usage` to `presets.ts` and cannot find `toolRenderers`; they chase '6 ctrl+o sites' and find 22, and assume the tree is broken rather than the plan.

gate:
Run the assertion script in `verification` verbatim from the repo root. DONE means it prints `failures: 0` and exits 0 — i.e. all 60 anchors in this ledger still resolve to the exact symbol they name, at HEAD 808b365.

The script is fail-able by construction, not by intent: 7 of the 60 assertions are the CORRECTED line numbers, which differ from the plan's. If an implementer had instead trusted the plan and written the assertions from IT, those 7 would go red on the first run — which is the point (verified: swapping 4 of them back to the plan's values yields exit 1 with exactly 4 FAIL). It also guards the tree moving under the ledger (e.g. `a usage-segment-end` fails the moment the usage segment grows or shrinks).

Explicitly OUT of scope for this gate: `bun test`, which cannot run (native addon absent). Do not add a test-file gate to a context item — there is no runtime behavior here to defend, and a placeholder test would violate AGENTS.md.

risk:
The risk is NOT that this ledger is wrong — every anchor in it was reproduced by a real command. The risk is that a later milestone section (which I did not read) re-derives the same claims from the PLAN instead of from this file, reintroducing the stale line numbers (7 of them are large enough to land in the wrong function — e.g. `interactive-mode.ts:6674` vs the real :6624, and the colorblind row pointing at `statusLineGit*` keys that have nothing to do with the token the branch adjusts) and the 3 wrong substantive claims. ctx2 is only useful if it is the single source of truth for M3 anchors, so the follow-on step is to fold these corrections back into COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_FOR_OMP_UPGRADE.md rather than leave two disagreeing documents.

The specific trap: three claims LOOK like minor numeric slips but are not. (a) '6 ctrl+o sites' is really 22 `expandKeyHint()` + 25 `formatExpandHint()` call sites — undercounting makes the row read as 'thin coverage' when it is saturation, which could prompt someone to build a redundant helper. (b) 'keyHint has no caller' is wrong; it has 4, and only `appKeyHint` is dead — B3's justification is weaker than the plan states. (c) the colorblind row cites statusLineGit* schema keys, which have nothing to do with the one token the branch actually adjusts; an engineer following it would edit the wrong part of the theme schema.
